paragraphs.title: Returning Lost Property and Helping Along the Way

easy.question: Which animals are mentioned in the first verse as examples of animals that have gone astray?
answers: An ox or a sheep
A donkey or a camel
A goat or a chicken
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thy brother’s ox or his sheep go astray.”

easy.question: What should you do when you find your brother’s animal?
answers: Leave it where it is
Return it to your brother
Sell it
easy.explanation: The verse commands, “Thou shalt in any case bring them again unto thy brother.”

easy.question: What should you do when you see your brother’s donkey or ox fallen on the road?
answers: Call only for the owner
Keep walking
Help him lift it up
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thou shalt surely help him to lift them up again.”

medium.question: What should you do if your brother is not near you and you do not know who he is?
answers: Bring the lost item home and keep it safely
Leave it on the road
Give it to the first person you meet
medium.explanation: The verse says to bring it home and keep it until your brother seeks it.

medium.question: What other things, besides an ox or a sheep, are included in the command?
answers: Only large animals
A donkey, clothing, and every lost thing
Only tools
medium.explanation: The verse extends the command to a donkey, clothing, and every lost thing belonging to your brother.

medium.question: In the phrase “go astray,” what does it mean that the animal has gone astray?
answers: It is sick
It is tied up
It is wandering or lost
medium.explanation: The phrase describes an animal that has wandered away, so it must be returned to its owner.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between the situations in verses 1–2 and the situation in verse 4?
answers: Verses 1–2 concern returning lost property, while verse 4 concerns helping an animal that has fallen
Verses 1–2 permit ignoring the problem, while verse 4 forbids it
Verses 1–2 concern only clothing, while verse 4 concerns only food
challenge.explanation: The first verses concern lost animals or objects, while verse 4 concerns helping a fallen animal.

challenge.question: What does the repeated command not to hide yourself emphasize?
answers: The command applies only when the owner asks for help
You must not avoid helping when you see lost property or an animal in distress
You may keep the lost item if it is valuable
challenge.explanation: The command emphasizes that you must act rather than ignore the situation.

challenge.question: Why must the lost item be kept at home even when the owner is unknown or far away?
answers: So you can use it until the owner comes
So no one has to search for the owner
So it is responsibly preserved until the owner claims it
challenge.explanation: The verse says to keep it “until thy brother seek after it.”

questions.question: What is the main difference between the situations in verses 1–2 and the situation in verse 4?
answers: Verses 1–2 concern returning lost property, while verse 4 concerns helping an animal that has fallen
Verses 1–2 permit ignoring the problem, while verse 4 forbids it
Verses 1–2 concern only clothing, while verse 4 concerns only food
questions.explanation: The first verses concern lost animals or objects, while verse 4 concerns helping a fallen animal.

questions.question: What does the repeated command not to hide yourself emphasize?
answers: The command applies only when the owner asks for help
You must not avoid helping when you see lost property or an animal in distress
You may keep the lost item if it is valuable
questions.explanation: The command emphasizes that you must act rather than ignore the situation.

questions.question: Why must the lost item be kept at home even when the owner is unknown or far away?
answers: So you can use it until the owner comes
So no one has to search for the owner
So it is responsibly preserved until the owner claims it
questions.explanation: The verse says to keep it “until thy brother seek after it.”

easy.question: What must a woman not wear according to the verse?
answers: That which pertains to a man
A woman’s garment
A priestly garment
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The woman shall not wear that which pertaineth unto a man.”

easy.question: What must a man not wear according to the verse?
answers: Weapons of war
A woman’s garment
A royal garment
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Neither shall a man put on a woman’s garment.”

easy.question: How does the verse describe those who do these things?
answers: As wise people
As brave people
As an abomination unto the LORD
easy.explanation: The verse calls these actions “abomination unto the LORD thy God.”

medium.question: What idea do the two prohibitions in the verse share?
answers: A ban on expensive clothing
A ban on wearing clothing associated with the opposite sex
A ban on clothing of a particular color
medium.explanation: The verse addresses both a woman wearing men’s clothing and a man wearing women’s clothing.

medium.question: What does “abomination” mean in the phrase “an abomination unto the LORD thy God”?
answers: Something especially desirable
Something ordinary
Something detestable
medium.explanation: “Abomination” describes something detestable in the sight of the LORD.

medium.question: Who is included in the phrase “all that do so”?
answers: Everyone who does the things described
Only women
Only leaders
medium.explanation: The word “all” includes anyone who does either of the prohibited actions.

challenge.question: What can be learned from the verse giving a separate prohibition for a woman and for a man?
answers: The prohibition applies only to women
The verse addresses both directions
Men are exempt from the prohibition
challenge.explanation: The verse mentions both a woman wearing men’s clothing and a man wearing women’s clothing.

challenge.question: What does “all that do so” refer to?
answers: Only women’s garments
All weapons
Both actions prohibited in the verse
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to both prohibited forms of dress.

challenge.question: What punishment does the verse explicitly state for the prohibited act?
answers: It does not specify a punishment here
It commands a fine
It commands the person to leave the land
challenge.explanation: The verse calls the act an abomination but does not state a specific practical punishment here.

questions.question: What can be learned from the verse giving a separate prohibition for a woman and for a man?
answers: The prohibition applies only to women
The verse addresses both directions
Men are exempt from the prohibition
questions.explanation: The verse mentions both a woman wearing men’s clothing and a man wearing women’s clothing.

questions.question: What does “all that do so” refer to?
answers: Only women’s garments
All weapons
Both actions prohibited in the verse
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to both prohibited forms of dress.

questions.question: What punishment does the verse explicitly state for the prohibited act?
answers: It does not specify a punishment here
It commands a fine
It commands the person to leave the land
questions.explanation: The verse calls the act an abomination but does not state a specific practical punishment here.

easy.question: What did the person find along the way?
answers: A bird’s nest
A flock of sheep
A spring of water
easy.explanation: The verse describes someone finding a bird’s nest along the way.

easy.question: Whom must you not take together with the young?
answers: The tree
The mother bird
The road
easy.explanation: The verse says not to take the mother with the young.

easy.question: What may you take after sending away the mother?
answers: Only the mother
The tree
The young
easy.explanation: After letting the mother go, the verse permits taking the young.

medium.question: Why does the Torah command that the mother be sent away before taking the young?
answers: So the mother is not taken together with her young
So the nest will fall
So another nest can be found
medium.explanation: Sending away the mother prevents taking her together with the young birds or eggs.

medium.question: In the phrase “the dam sitting upon the young,” what does “sitting” mean?
answers: Flying in the sky
Sitting or resting on them
Looking for food
medium.explanation: The context shows that the mother is resting on the young or eggs.

medium.question: What is the correct order of actions according to the verses?
answers: Take the young, find the nest, and send away the mother
Send away the mother, find the nest, and take the young
Find the nest, send away the mother, and take the young
medium.explanation: First the nest is found, then the mother is sent away, and finally the young may be taken.

challenge.question: Where may the bird’s nest be found according to the verse?
answers: Only inside a house
In a tree or on the ground
Only on a roof
challenge.explanation: The verse mentions a nest in any tree or on the ground.

challenge.question: What does the repeated phrase “thou shalt in any wise let the dam go” emphasize?
answers: Sending away the mother is an emphasized command
Two mothers must be taken
The young must not be taken
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that the mother must be released.

challenge.question: What result is promised to the person who keeps this command?
answers: Wealth and honor
Victory in war
Well-being and long life
challenge.explanation: The verse promises, “that it may be well with thee, and that thou mayest prolong thy days.”

questions.question: Where may the bird’s nest be found according to the verse?
answers: Only inside a house
In a tree or on the ground
Only on a roof
questions.explanation: The verse mentions a nest in any tree or on the ground.

questions.question: What does the repeated phrase “thou shalt in any wise let the dam go” emphasize?
answers: Sending away the mother is an emphasized command
Two mothers must be taken
The young must not be taken
questions.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that the mother must be released.

questions.question: What result is promised to the person who keeps this command?
answers: Wealth and honor
Victory in war
Well-being and long life
questions.explanation: The verse promises, “that it may be well with thee, and that thou mayest prolong thy days.”

easy.question: What does the Torah command you to do to the roof of a new house?
answers: Build a battlement on it
Paint it
Cover it with dirt
easy.explanation: The Torah commands, “thou shalt make a battlement for thy roof.”

easy.question: What danger does the Torah want to prevent?
answers: Loss of property
A person falling from the roof
A fire in the house
easy.explanation: The battlement is meant to prevent someone from falling from the roof.

easy.question: What kind of house is mentioned at the beginning of the verse?
answers: An old house
A public building
A new house
easy.explanation: The verse begins, “When thou buildest a new house.”

medium.question: What is a battlement in the phrase “thou shalt make a battlement for thy roof”?
answers: A safety barrier or railing
A large window
Stairs to the roof
medium.explanation: A battlement is a barrier around the roof intended to prevent falls.

medium.question: Why must a battlement be made on the roof?
answers: To make the house look more attractive
To prevent someone from falling
To increase the size of the house
medium.explanation: The Torah requires it because someone might fall from the roof.

medium.question: What sequence of events is described in the verse?
answers: Someone falls, and then the house is built
A house is built, a battlement is made, and danger is prevented
A battlement is made, the house is destroyed, and then a roof is built
medium.explanation: After building a new house, a battlement is installed to prevent a fall.

challenge.question: What is the practical meaning of “that thou bring not blood upon thine house”?
answers: Water must not be brought into the house
The house may not be used at night
The owner must ensure that the house is not a place of danger
challenge.explanation: The warning requires the owner to prevent danger that could cause injury or death.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the words “if any man fall from thence”?
answers: The battlement protects against a possible danger before an accident occurs
Only someone who has already fallen must build one
The roof is only for people who know how to climb
challenge.explanation: The command requires preparing in advance for the possibility of a fall.

challenge.question: What broader principle can be learned from the command about the battlement?
answers: A property owner is responsible for taking safety measures to protect others
Only professionals are responsible for safety
Danger in a house is not the owner’s responsibility
challenge.explanation: The command places practical responsibility on the owner to prevent harm.

questions.question: What is the practical meaning of “that thou bring not blood upon thine house”?
answers: Water must not be brought into the house
The house may not be used at night
The owner must ensure that the house is not a place of danger
questions.explanation: The warning requires the owner to prevent danger that could cause injury or death.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the words “if any man fall from thence”?
answers: The battlement protects against a possible danger before an accident occurs
Only someone who has already fallen must build one
The roof is only for people who know how to climb
questions.explanation: The command requires preparing in advance for the possibility of a fall.

questions.question: What broader principle can be learned from the command about the battlement?
answers: A property owner is responsible for taking safety measures to protect others
Only professionals are responsible for safety
Danger in a house is not the owner’s responsibility
questions.explanation: The command places practical responsibility on the owner to prevent harm.

paragraphs.title: The Prohibition of Mixed Seed in a Vineyard

easy.question: What must not be done in a vineyard according to the verse?
answers: Sow it with different kinds of seed
Water it
Gather its grapes
easy.explanation: The verse forbids sowing a vineyard with different kinds of seed.

easy.question: What may happen if different seeds are sown in a vineyard?
answers: The vineyard will grow faster
The seed and the produce may be defiled
The grapes will become sweeter
easy.explanation: The verse warns that both the seed and the vineyard’s produce may be defiled.

easy.question: What place is specifically mentioned as one where mixed seed must not be sown?
answers: A wheat field
A garden
A vineyard
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thou shalt not sow thy vineyard with divers seeds.”

medium.question: Why does the Torah warn against sowing different kinds of seed in a vineyard?
answers: Because the produce may be defiled
Because the vineyard will receive no water
Because the grapes will disappear
medium.explanation: The verse gives the concern that the seed and the vineyard’s produce may be defiled.

medium.question: In the phrase “lest the fruit of thy seed,” what does “lest” express?
answers: Perhaps
A warning to prevent something
Immediately
medium.explanation: “Lest” introduces a warning about a possible result of sowing mixed seed.

medium.question: What may be affected by sowing mixed seed in a vineyard?
answers: Only the soil
Only the grapes
The seed that is sown and the vineyard’s produce
medium.explanation: The verse mentions both the seed that is sown and the fruit of the vineyard.

challenge.question: What is the connection between the prohibition and the word “defiled” in the verse?
answers: The mixed produce may acquire a prohibited or special status
The vineyard will become a place of prayer
The seeds will not sprout at all
challenge.explanation: The warning is based on the possibility that the mixed produce will be defiled.

challenge.question: What can be learned from the order of ideas in the verse?
answers: Harvesting comes before sowing
Sowing in a vineyard may affect both the seed and the vineyard’s produce
Only the vineyard’s produce causes a problem, not the seed
challenge.explanation: The verse links the act of sowing with consequences for both the seed and the crop.

challenge.question: Which distinction is accurate according to the verse?
answers: The prohibition concerns every mixture of foods
The prohibition concerns only harvesting grapes
The prohibition concerns sowing mixed seed in a vineyard
challenge.explanation: The verse focuses on sowing mixed seed in a vineyard, not on all food mixtures or on harvesting itself.

questions.question: What is the connection between the prohibition and the word “defiled” in the verse?
answers: The mixed produce may acquire a prohibited or special status
The vineyard will become a place of prayer
The seeds will not sprout at all
questions.explanation: The warning is based on the possibility that the mixed produce will be defiled.

questions.question: What can be learned from the order of ideas in the verse?
answers: Harvesting comes before sowing
Sowing in a vineyard may affect both the seed and the vineyard’s produce
Only the vineyard’s produce causes a problem, not the seed
questions.explanation: The verse links the act of sowing with consequences for both the seed and the crop.

questions.question: Which distinction is accurate according to the verse?
answers: The prohibition concerns every mixture of foods
The prohibition concerns only harvesting grapes
The prohibition concerns sowing mixed seed in a vineyard
questions.explanation: The verse focuses on sowing mixed seed in a vineyard, not on all food mixtures or on harvesting itself.

paragraphs.title: Do Not Plow with an Ox and a Donkey Together

easy.question: Which two animals must not be used together for plowing?
answers: An ox and a donkey
A sheep and a goat
A horse and a camel
easy.explanation: The verse specifically forbids plowing with an ox and a donkey together.

easy.question: What is forbidden according to the verse?
answers: Watering animals
Plowing with an ox and a donkey together
Raising an ox and a donkey
easy.explanation: The command forbids using the two animals together for plowing.

easy.question: What does “together” mean in the verse?
answers: At night
From a distance
At the same time or as a pair
easy.explanation: The verse prohibits the ox and donkey from plowing together.

medium.question: What activity links the ox and the donkey in the verse?
answers: They are offered as one sacrifice
They work together in plowing
They live in the same pen
medium.explanation: The verse concerns an ox and a donkey harnessed together for fieldwork.

medium.question: Which action is explicitly forbidden?
answers: Buying an ox and a donkey
Feeding an ox and a donkey
Plowing with an ox and a donkey together
medium.explanation: The prohibition is not ownership or feeding, but plowing with them together.

medium.question: Why is it clear that the verse refers to two animals working together?
answers: Because plowing is mentioned
Because their dwelling place is mentioned
Because harvest time is mentioned
medium.explanation: The verb “plow” shows that the animals are harnessed for fieldwork.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from prohibiting an ox and a donkey from plowing together?
answers: No animals may be used for work
An ox and a donkey have equal strength
An unsuitable pairing should not be forced into shared work
challenge.explanation: The prohibition concerns this particular pairing, suggesting that animals should be suited to working together.

challenge.question: Which detail emphasizes that the prohibition concerns a shared action?
answers: The word “together”
The word “ox”
The word “plow”
challenge.explanation: “Together” emphasizes that both animals would be involved in the same plowing.

challenge.question: What ethical meaning may be suggested by the command?
answers: The donkey should always be preferred to the ox
The animals’ abilities and condition should be taken into account
Only large animals should be used
challenge.explanation: The command may teach consideration for animals and the differences between them.

questions.question: What can be inferred from prohibiting an ox and a donkey from plowing together?
answers: No animals may be used for work
An ox and a donkey have equal strength
An unsuitable pairing should not be forced into shared work
questions.explanation: The prohibition concerns this particular pairing, suggesting that animals should be suited to working together.

questions.question: Which detail emphasizes that the prohibition concerns a shared action?
answers: The word “together”
The word “ox”
The word “plow”
questions.explanation: “Together” emphasizes that both animals would be involved in the same plowing.

questions.question: What ethical meaning may be suggested by the command?
answers: The donkey should always be preferred to the ox
The animals’ abilities and condition should be taken into account
Only large animals should be used
questions.explanation: The command may teach consideration for animals and the differences between them.

easy.question: What must not be worn according to the verse?
answers: A garment of mixed fabric
A dyed garment
A woolen garment
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thou shalt not wear a garment of divers sorts.”

easy.question: Which two materials are mentioned in the verse?
answers: Cotton and leather
Wool and linen
Silk and cotton
easy.explanation: The verse specifically mentions wool and linen.

easy.question: What does “together” mean in the verse?
answers: Separately
Rarely
Combined with one another
easy.explanation: It means that wool and linen are combined in the same garment.

medium.question: What makes wool and linen a problem according to the verse?
answers: When they are worn together in one garment
When they are kept in a house
When they are dyed the same color
medium.explanation: The prohibition concerns wearing wool and linen together.

medium.question: What does “a garment of divers sorts” mean in this context?
answers: A leather garment
A garment made only of wool
A garment combining wool and linen
medium.explanation: The verse explains that the mixed garment consists of wool and linen together.

medium.question: What does the word “together” show?
answers: All kinds of fabric are forbidden
The prohibition concerns combining the two materials
Only wool clothing may be worn
medium.explanation: The word shows that the issue is the combination of wool and linen.

challenge.question: Which situation is not described as forbidden in the verse?
answers: Wearing a garment combining wool and linen
Wearing a garment made only of wool
Wearing a mixed-fabric garment
challenge.explanation: The verse forbids wool and linen together; it does not say that wool alone is forbidden.

challenge.question: Which word shows that the command concerns a person’s action?
answers: Wool
Linen
Wear
challenge.explanation: “Wear” is the verb describing the person’s action.

challenge.question: What detail might be missed when reading the verse?
answers: The prohibition is on wool and linen together, not on each material separately
The prohibition concerns only a particular color
The prohibition concerns making clothing only
challenge.explanation: The word “together” shows that the key issue is combining the two materials.

questions.question: Which situation is not described as forbidden in the verse?
answers: Wearing a garment combining wool and linen
Wearing a garment made only of wool
Wearing a mixed-fabric garment
questions.explanation: The verse forbids wool and linen together; it does not say that wool alone is forbidden.

questions.question: Which word shows that the command concerns a person’s action?
answers: Wool
Linen
Wear
questions.explanation: “Wear” is the verb describing the person’s action.

questions.question: What detail might be missed when reading the verse?
answers: The prohibition is on wool and linen together, not on each material separately
The prohibition concerns only a particular color
The prohibition concerns making clothing only
questions.explanation: The word “together” shows that the key issue is combining the two materials.

paragraphs.title: Fringes on the Corners of a Garment

easy.question: What must be made on the corners of the garment?
answers: Fringes
Dye
Pockets
easy.explanation: The verse commands, “Thou shalt make thee fringes.”

easy.question: On how many corners of the garment must fringes be made?
answers: Two corners
Four corners
Six corners
easy.explanation: The verse says, “upon the four quarters of thy vesture.”

easy.question: What is the garment used for?
answers: Covering oneself
Storing food
Building a tent
easy.explanation: It is the garment “wherewith thou coverest thyself.”

medium.question: If the garment has four corners, what must be done?
answers: Make only one fringe
Make fringes on all four corners
Remove the garment
medium.explanation: The command connects the four corners with making fringes on them.

medium.question: What are the “four quarters” of the garment?
answers: Its corners or edges
Its sleeves
Its buttons
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the corners or ends of the garment.

medium.question: What connection is there between the garment and the command about fringes?
answers: The fringes are made on a garment used for covering oneself
The fringes replace the garment
The garment is used only to store the fringes
medium.explanation: The verse commands fringes on the garment with which a person covers himself.

challenge.question: What precise detail is easy to overlook in the verse?
answers: The fringes are made on four corners
The fringes are made on only one corner
The fringes are made on the head
challenge.explanation: The verse specifies both the number four and the location—the corners of the garment.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “wherewith thou coverest thyself”?
answers: It is a garment for personal use
It is forbidden to wear
It is intended for trade
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that the person uses the garment to cover himself.

challenge.question: What does the command not specify?
answers: The color of the fringes
Where the fringes are made
The number of corners
challenge.explanation: The verse specifies the location and number but not the color.

questions.question: What precise detail is easy to overlook in the verse?
answers: The fringes are made on four corners
The fringes are made on only one corner
The fringes are made on the head
questions.explanation: The verse specifies both the number four and the location—the corners of the garment.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “wherewith thou coverest thyself”?
answers: It is a garment for personal use
It is forbidden to wear
It is intended for trade
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that the person uses the garment to cover himself.

questions.question: What does the command not specify?
answers: The color of the fringes
Where the fringes are made
The number of corners
questions.explanation: The verse specifies the location and number but not the color.

paragraphs.title: A False Accusation Against a Woman

easy.question: What did the man claim about his wife?
answers: That he had not found her a virgin
That she had stolen his money
That she had left the city
easy.explanation: The man claimed that he had not found her a virgin.

easy.question: Who brought the evidence before the elders of the city?
answers: The man and his brothers
The girl’s father and mother
The girl’s neighbors
easy.explanation: Her father and mother brought the tokens of her virginity to the elders.

easy.question: What was the penalty for the man who brought up an evil name against her?
answers: He was expelled from the city
He paid ten shekels
He paid one hundred shekels
easy.explanation: He had to pay one hundred shekels to the girl’s father.

medium.question: Why did the girl’s father and mother go to the elders of the city?
answers: To ask the man for a gift
To present evidence and defend her reputation
To return the girl to their home
medium.explanation: They presented evidence to prove that the man’s accusation was false.

medium.question: What does “bring up an evil name upon her” mean in this context?
answers: Speak words of praise
Write the marriage contract
Make false accusations against her
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to spreading a false accusation that damaged her reputation.

medium.question: What follows from the fact that the man was punished and could not put away his wife?
answers: He had to remain married to her
He could divorce her immediately
The marriage ended automatically
medium.explanation: The verses impose both a fine and a lifelong prohibition against sending her away.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the accusation was not accepted solely on the man’s word?
answers: He said that he hated her
He had married her previously
Her parents brought evidence before the elders
challenge.explanation: Her parents brought evidence to the elders, so the matter was examined rather than decided only by his claim.

challenge.question: Why was the payment given specifically to the girl’s father?
answers: Because the man had brought up an evil name against his daughter
Because the father had already paid the fine
Because the father was one of the elders
challenge.explanation: The payment went to the father because the man had damaged his daughter’s reputation.

challenge.question: What is unusual about the final result of the case?
answers: The girl is sent to another city
The man may not put away his wife all his days
The elders become witnesses to the marriage
challenge.explanation: In addition to the fine, the man is forbidden to divorce her for the rest of his life.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the accusation was not accepted solely on the man’s word?
answers: He said that he hated her
He had married her previously
Her parents brought evidence before the elders
questions.explanation: Her parents brought evidence to the elders, so the matter was examined rather than decided only by his claim.

questions.question: Why was the payment given specifically to the girl’s father?
answers: Because the man had brought up an evil name against his daughter
Because the father had already paid the fine
Because the father was one of the elders
questions.explanation: The payment went to the father because the man had damaged his daughter’s reputation.

questions.question: What is unusual about the final result of the case?
answers: The girl is sent to another city
The man may not put away his wife all his days
The elders become witnesses to the marriage
questions.explanation: In addition to the fine, the man is forbidden to divorce her for the rest of his life.

paragraphs.title: The Case of a Girl Found Guilty

easy.question: What was found if the man’s claim about the girl was true?
answers: The girl was not found to be a virgin
The girl had fled from home
The girl confessed
easy.explanation: The verse says that the tokens of virginity were not found.

easy.question: Where was the girl taken?
answers: To the city gate
To the door of her father’s house
To the priest’s house
easy.explanation: The verse says she was brought to the door of her father’s house.

easy.question: Who stoned the girl?
answers: The elders of Israel
Her family members
The men of her city
easy.explanation: The verse says, “the men of her city shall stone her.”

medium.question: What is the order of events in the verse?
answers: The men stone the girl, and then she is brought out
The girl is brought to her father’s door, and then the men stone her
The girl leaves the city, and then they return her
medium.explanation: First she is brought to her father’s door, and afterward the men of the city stone her.

medium.question: According to the verse, why is the severe punishment imposed?
answers: Because she committed folly in Israel and played the harlot in her father’s house
Because she did not want to live in the city
Because she hid her property from her family
medium.explanation: The verse gives those acts as the reason for the punishment.

medium.question: What does “folly” mean in the phrase “she hath wrought folly in Israel”?
answers: An expensive gift
A serious illness
